next_step: Run 2-week POC: JetBrains plugin + dedicated pool; benchmark streaming 99th-pct latency; follow up security questionnaire; schedule dev handoff
notes:
Sales/Technical notes (shorthand):
- Intro call 2025-11-12 w/ CTO (N. Patel) + Head of Eng (L. Romero). Interested in a JetBrains (IntelliJ/PyCharm) plugin as primary UX for their internal devs.
- Primary ask: low-latency code completions + streaming suggestions in-editor. Local indexing of monorepo on developer machines to enable contextual completions without sending all source off-host.
- Privacy: cannot send private repo contents to third-party hosted models by default. Prefer VPC or on-prem controller + local prefix indexing (client-side).
- Model requirements: want ability to pin model versions per workspace (dev vs CI) and fallback routing (smaller quantized model for quick completions, larger model for complex refactors). Mentioned: "must be able to pin to quantized open-models".
- Performance SLOs discussed: target interactive latency: 50-150ms p50, 95ms-120ms p90 for single-line completion; 99th-pct streaming latency target under 250ms for 30 concurrent devs in dedicated pool. SE asked about batching impact on interactivity.
- Caching/indexing: they plan to run a local indexer that provides short prefix vectors (embedding cache) to the plugin; Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching + cache) could reduce infra cost. They want deterministic fallback to hosted model when local index misses.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + ISO27001 needed for production; require KMS integration for keys, audit logs for token-level access, SSO/SAML for plugin auth, retention controls and option for EU-only residency for some teams.
- Deployment preference: start on Dedicated (reserved capacity) in a customer VPC, then evaluate Private on-prem for R&D teams with air-gapped workflows.
- POC scope proposed: 2-week bench + 1-week integration:
   * Week 0: plugin dev handoff + repo access (read-only).
   * Week 1: deploy dedicated pool, baseline latency tests (p50/p90/p99) for single-line completion and multi-line refactor flows.
   * Week 2: local index integration (dev-machine indexer) + streaming tests; measure cost per 1k tokens and cache hit ratio.
   * Acceptance criteria: <120ms p90 single-line completions, streaming start <200ms at 8 concurrent, plugin auth via SSO + audit logs present.
- Timeline: security questionnaire sent 2026-02-10 (legal); awaiting answers from their SecOps (target EOD 2026-02-22). AE note: "CTO wants to see live demo inside IntelliJ before exec sign-off."
- Meeting refs: Fireflies ff-20260208-jetforge-integration (dev session), internal thread thread-CAFE1234-jetforge-poc.
- Pricing: estimated ARR ask ~50k-200k depending on dedicated capacity and support SLAs.
- Quote from CTO: "We can't compromise dev flow latency — if it feels slow we won't adopt."
- Next actions (short): schedule SE plugin deep-dive (Miguel), provide security SOW & dedicated pool sizing, confirm marketplace/distribution licensing for JetBrains plugin.
- Notes on competition: they also trialed Tabnine (saw 30% cheaper but worse accuracy on large-refactor prompts); GitHub Copilot blocked by internal IP policy.
- Misc: Customer interested in Redwood's model pinning + rollout (canary) features to test different quantized variants across teams.
